what_it_does: IRIS is a specialized processor (system-on-a-chip, or SoC) built to run real-time 3D Gaussian Splatting—a technique for rendering interactive 3D scenes by splatting Gaussian blobs across a 2D image. The chip targets spatial computing applications like AR/VR where you need to render and understand 3D scenes in real-time on a mobile or edge device. The paper achieves very low energy consumption (8.55 millijoules per rendered frame), which is important for battery-powered spatial computing devices. The architecture combines specialized pipelines for rasterization (turning geometry into pixels), differentiable rendering (math that learns from rendered output), and surface modeling (reconstructing the 3D shape from visual observations).
